To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the system loss factor of a multilayers cylindrical shell with elastic and/or viscoelastic layers increases with increasing number of layers and (ii) for a given number of layers, the system loss factor decreases with increasing thickness of viscoelastic layers.

the system loss factor is a strong function of the mode number and the damping characteristics of the shell, that the damping effectiveness of the shell is strongly dependent on the shell thickness, the number of layers, and the damping characteristics and that the loss factor of the shell is not significantly affected by the elastic modulus of the material layers.

(1) the system loss factor increases with the number of elastic layers in the shell, and (2) for a fixed number of elastic layers the system loss factor decreases with an increase in the number of viscoelastic layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical study and numerical analysis of the vibration and damping behavior of a multilayers cylindrical shell with elastic and/or viscoelastic layers.
the vibration and damping analysis of multilayered composite cylindrical shells with arbitrary number of layers and with the effects of the viscoelastic layers.
the vibration and damping analysis of multilayered shells with elastic and viscoleastic layers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results obtained from the present analysis are in good agreement with those obtained from the classical shell theory and the finite element analysis.

the present analysis is a generalization of the previous work and that the results are valid for all types of cylindrical shells, including the sandwich type, and for all types of boundary conditions, including the simply supported and clamped types.

the damping effectiveness of the viscoelastic layers increases with increasing frequency, and that the viscoelastic layer damping effectiveness is greater than that of the viscoelastically bonded layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present work is the first to consider the vibration and damping analysis of general multilayer cylindrical shells with arbitrary number of elastic and viscoelatic layers.
the results obtained from the present analysis are in excellent agreement with the results of the previous analyses for a single orthotropic layer.
a general procedure for determining the vibration characteristics of a multilayers shell with an arbitrary number of elastic and visco-elastic layers has been presented.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the damping effectiveness of a viscoelastic layer can be increased substantially if the viscoelastic layer is placed near the shell midplane.
, for a given material system, the damping effectiveness of multilayered shells is greater than that of a homogeneous shell of the same thickness.

the system loss factor can be increased by increasing the number of viscoelastic layers, by increasing the thickness of the viscoelastic layers and by increasing the loss factor of the viscoelasticty layers.
